title: Newton's first law and equilibrium; Inertial frames
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Mechanics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: K05-ap1#t2 term and clue written for the game; D02-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; D02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; K05-ap1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D02-1#N.2, K05-ap1#N.2, D02-1#N.4, K05-ap1#N.5, D02-1#N.11, K05-ap1#N.6.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Newton's first law
items.clue: Statement that zero net force means constant velocity, possibly zero.

items.label: Equilibrium
items.clue: State of a body, such as a steadily falling skydiver, whose forces balance.

items.label: Terminal velocity
items.clue: Constant value a skydiver's downward motion settles at once drag equals weight.

items.label: Inertial frame
items.clue: Viewpoint in which the rule about zero net force holds; the ground, for everyday motion.

questions.stem: A space probe is so far from any star or planet that the forces exerted on it are negligible. Its engines fire briefly and then shut off. Which statement describes the probe's motion after the engines have shut off?

options.text: It slows down and stops, as all moving objects do in time.
It slows down as the force from the engine firing is used up.
It moves in a straight line at a constant speed.
It stops almost at once, as no force now pushes it forward.

questions.stem: A train is at rest on a straight, level track. A ball rests on the smooth floor of one of its train cars; friction and air resistance are negligible. The train then starts to speed up forward, and a passenger sees the ball slide toward the back of the train car, although no horizontal force is exerted on the ball. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The train car is not an inertial frame while the train speeds up.
A backward force caused by the train's motion is exerted on the ball.
The train car is an inertial frame, as the train moves in a straight line.
No moving vehicle is an inertial frame, even one at constant velocity.

questions.stem: A puck slides east at constant velocity across level ice with negligible friction. Starting at time t, a constant force directed north is exerted on the puck, and no other horizontal force acts. Which statement describes the puck's motion after time t?

options.text: It turns and moves due north, in the direction of the force on it.
Its eastward velocity decreases while its northward velocity increases.
It moves at a constant velocity in a direction between east and north.
Its eastward velocity stays the same while its northward velocity increases.

questions.stem: Treat the ground as an inertial frame. Which of these is also an inertial frame?

options.text: A car braking steadily from 20 m s⁻¹ to a stop at a red light
A merry-go-round turning at a steady rate of one turn every 10 s
An airplane flying straight and level at a steady 250 m s⁻¹
An elevator speeding up steadily as it leaves the ground floor

questions.explanation: Straight, level flight at a steady speed is constant velocity relative to the ground. A frame moving at constant velocity relative to an inertial frame is itself inertial, however fast it moves.

questions.stem: Which of the following objects is in translational equilibrium?

options.text: A ball at the top of its flight, momentarily at rest
A car rounding a curve on a level road at a constant speed
A puck slowing down on rough ice after a stick stops pushing it
A crate riding up a straight conveyor at a steady 2 m s⁻¹

questions.explanation: Its speed and direction are both constant, so its velocity is constant and the net force on it is zero: friction from the belt, up the slope, balances the component of its weight down the slope, and the normal force balances the rest.

questions.stem: A car rounds a level bend at a constant speed. A can rests on the car's smooth, frictionless dashboard. A passenger sees the can slide toward the outside of the bend, although no horizontal force is exerted on it. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A force on the can pushes it toward the outside of the bend.
The car is not an inertial frame: its velocity is changing.
The car is an inertial frame, since its speed stays constant.
Newton's first law does not apply to objects inside vehicles.

questions.explanation: Velocity has a direction. Turning changes the car's velocity even at constant speed, so the car accelerates and is not an inertial frame. From the road, an inertial frame, the can obeys the first law: it moves in a straight line at constant speed.
